I'm going to first discuss Risk of Rain Returns as a remake, and then as a game. 

Risk of Rain Returns is, in my opinion, the definitive way to play the now classic indie roguelike. It is that unfortunately rare type of remake whose changes enhance the original rather than modifying it. It adds new challenges, items, enemies and characters along with beautiful pixel art that does thankfully look like an HD version of the original. It also fixed the multiplayer so you don't have to port forward anymore ([i]hallelujah[/i]) and other technical problems. I wish all remakes were like this.

Now, what actually is Risk of Rain Returns? It is a side-scrolling roguelike in which you, an insignificant survivor of a ship attack, have to get off Petrichor V. You need to collect dropped cargo to make yourself stronger, and you'd better hurry because the planet is starting to notice your presence and it wants you gone. It isn't a super mechanically complex game. A sidescroller in which you have 4 abilities and an active limited by cooldowns unique to each character, you run across a stage full of constantly respawning enemies looking for the exit to the next level before needing to do a last stand and fight a boss for that stage. Despite the simplicity the variety keeps runs feeling fresh and the large quantity of unlocks give you stuff to keep playing towards. Chris Christodoulou's now iconic soundtrack returns, blending with the lovely art style better than ever before.

I highly recommend Risk of Rain Return for both newcomers to the series and returning veterans alike.

I did not expect this game to be this much fun or addicting. I generally don't play many rogue-lites (or whatever the genre here is) but the gameplay loop is simple and loads of fun. Maybe its the 2D platforming that drew me in but the art style here is also superb.
